title.value: Leveraging Observations in Bandits: Between Risks and Benefits
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Leveraging Observations in Bandits: Between Risks and Benefits

analysis.description: The paper explores the concept of observational learning in the context of multi-armed bandits, proposing a new optimism modifier called Target-UCB that leverages actions observed from a target policy, even when associated rewards are not visible. The study provides theoretical analysis and empirical results to show both advantages and limitations of this approach.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments and provides empirical results to validate the proposed model, indicating that it is empirical research.
type.quote: We provide empirical results showing both great benefits as well as certain limitations inherent to observational learning in the multi-armed bandit setting.

name.justification: The paper focuses on bandits, a common problem setting within reinforcement learning, and discusses learning from observations, which is a reinforcement learning concept.
name.quote: In this work, we study the observational learning problem in the context of bandits, the simplest setting for studying the explore-exploit trade-off faced by an agent in an unknown environment.

name.justification: The paper specifically addresses the observational learning problem within the context of multi-armed bandits, using algorithms like Upper Confidence Bound.
name.quote: In this work, we study the observational learning problem in the context of bandits, the simplest setting for studying the explore-exploit trade-off faced by an agent in an unknown environment.

name.justification: Target-UCB is the main model introduced and analyzed in the paper to incorporate observational learning into the UCB algorithm.
name.quote: By adding target optimism (Equation 2) to the UCB algorithm, we obtain a new variant: Target-UCB.

is_contributed.justification: The paper introduces Target-UCB as a new contribution, specifically modifying the UCB algorithm for the study.
is_contributed.quote: By adding target optimism (Equation 2) to the UCB algorithm, we obtain a new variant: Target-UCB.

is_executed.justification: The paper includes empirical results and experiments conducted using the Target-UCB model.
is_executed.quote: We provide empirical results showing both great benefits as well as certain limitations inherent to observational learning in the multi-armed bandit setting.

is_compared.justification: Target-UCB is compared to a baseline algorithm and other strategies to highlight its performance advantages and limitations.
is_compared.quote: We also notice that the greedy follower baseline performs even better. This is not surprising as the considered target (UCB) is good (and improving).
